blocks.content: Japanese has no spaces between words. Word boundaries are legible because the three scripts alternate predictably, and because readers have internalised the grammar. The punctuation system is its own, parallel to the Western one.

rows.name: Touten
rows.use: Comma : marks a pause within a sentence

rows.name: Nijū kagikakko
rows.use: Nested quotation marks, or book and work titles

rows.name: Nakaguro
rows.use: Separates list items or parts of a foreign name

rows.name: Chōonpu
rows.use: Extends a vowel sound in katakana words

rows.name: Full-width forms
rows.use: Same function as English, but full-width for alignment

blocks.content: In Japanese fiction and manga, 「」kagikakko are the standard dialogue markers : not Western-style quotation marks. You will encounter them constantly in native texts.

rows.japanese: 私はりんご、みかん、ぶどうを買いました。
rows.romaji: Watashi wa ringo, mikan, budō wo kaimashita.
rows.english: I bought apples, oranges, and grapes.

blocks.content: Modern Japanese is written horizontally, left to right. Traditional texts : novels, some newspapers, manga speech bubbles : run *vertically* in columns read right to left. Both directions are in active use today.
